Q: A man travelling on a straight line moves with a uniform velocity v1 for a distance x and
with a uniform velocity v2 for the next equal distance. Find the average velocity.
Solution: Let x be the distance, t1 and t2 be the time for the respective velocities v1 and v2.
Then average velocity, v = x+x = x x 2x ⇒ v = 1 1 2
Instantaneous Velocity
The velocity at any point and at any instant of time is the instantaneous velocity. It is written
as V = lim = ∆s = ds ∆t dt Δ t → 0
The instantaneous velocity indicates the velocity at every possible point at any instant of
time.

Acceleration:

Think of the following Facts: ● A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 50 ms-1. After 1 second the velocity decreases to 40 ms-1. Another second later it decreases further to 30 ms-1. By the end of the third second, the velocity is 20 ms-1, and by the fourth second, it decreases to 10 ms-1. Finally, after the fifth second, the velocity becomes zero, and the
ball begins to fall back down, after spending a total of 5 seconds in the air.
As the ball falls, its velocity increases by 10 ms-1 each second, reaching a striking velocity of 50 ms-1 when it hits the ground after 5 seconds.
● Consider why there is a consistent change in velocity by an equal amount after each
second elapses. What are your thoughts on this uniform change in velocity occurring
every second?
The change in velocity in each second is known as acceleration, which can either be
an increase or a decrease in velocity. When there is a decrease in velocity in each second, it is referred to as deceleration or negative acceleration.
Therefore, acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity.
